name: Acid reflux (GERD)
surveyQuestion: Do you have any of these health conditions? (select all that apply) -> Acid reflux / GERD. Check: Has a doctor told you that you have GERD or acid reflux? Yes, GERD / Yes, on regular acid medicine (PPI or similar) / Heartburn sometimes, not diagnosed / Not sure (see a doctor) / No. Red-flag screen first: trouble or pain swallowing, weight loss without trying, repeated vomiting, black stools or vomiting blood, low haemoglobin or anaemia, new symptoms after age 50, chest pain, symptoms for more than 2 weeks despite lifestyle changes.

waterMl.notes: No change from the general FitPlate range (topic 30: 2,500 ml men, 2,000 ml women). Sip between meals and avoid large volumes with meals or just before lying down (est.). Plain still water is fine; fizzy water and soft drinks lower sphincter pressure in small studies, so limit if they trigger symptoms. In heat or exercise follow topic 31 (cap 4,500, est.). With kidney, heart or liver disease, pregnancy, a fluid limit or a diuretic show the general range only. Follow your doctor's advice.

conflictsWith.rule: Calcium carbonate antacids add calcium on top of food: stone formers ask a doctor first; fluid goal stays doctor-led (P14)
ENO, baking soda and effervescent antacids carry sodium; keep sodium under 2,000 mg (P3, topic 18)
Doctor sets fluids, sodium, magnesium and calcium; antacids with magnesium, aluminium or calcium need doctor input (P13)
Pregnancy heartburn is common; doctor chooses any medicine; app shows lifestyle tips only (P22)
Weight loss is the best-supported reflux measure if overweight, but no crash diets or long fasts; keep dinner earlier and smaller (P25)
Low-FODMAP and GERD trigger lists can clash (onion, garlic); change one thing at a time with a dietitian (P16)
Anaemia with reflux is an alarm feature: doctor first; acid medicine can reduce iron absorption (P11)

warnings: GERD is diagnosed by a doctor; FitPlate gives general food and habit information only

Red flags: trouble or pain swallowing, weight loss without trying, repeated vomiting, black stools or vomiting blood, anaemia, new symptoms after age 50, chest pain (rule out heart cause first), symptoms lasting more than 2 weeks despite lifestyle changes: see a doctor before any diet plan
Never advise on PPIs, H2 blockers, antacid doses, stopping or starting medicines
Calcium carbonate antacids: stay within label directions; very large amounts can cause high calcium (calcium-alkali syndrome); stone formers ask a doctor
ENO and baking soda contain sodium (about 0.7-0.85 g sodium per 4.3-5 g sachet, label-dependent); avoid regular use with high BP, heart, kidney or liver disease
Ayurvedic powders and churnas: no GERD evidence found; some Indian-made products had lead or mercury in a 2004 JAMA study of 70 products; ask a doctor
Pregnancy and infants: doctor; infants are out of scope
